listings.expertise:

listings.name: Ananta Yoga
listings.description:
Build Inner Balance Workshop for People living with Parkinson’s

Discover evidence-based techniques for inner well-being

Join us for a 3-session online program that offers simple, research-supported yogic practices to help people living with Parkinson’s reduce stress and anxiety, calm the nervous system and enhance inner wellbeing. Through gentle breathing practices, sound yoga, and guided meditation, participants learn powerful tools to support mental health, emotional stability, relaxation, and inner peace. These methods are safe, practical, and easy to integrate into daily life.

This program is open to:

– Individuals with Parkinson’s.
– Family members and care partners who wish to learn supportive techniques for relaxation and balance

Over three sessions, you’ll learn:

– A 4-minute breathing technique to enhance energy and focus
– Sound yoga to improve stability and mental clarity
– A 12-minute guided meditation to promote relaxation and inner balance

Each practice is designed to be gentle, accessible, and effective for daily use.

Find out more and register online at: https://anantayoga.life/balance
listings.expertise:
Scientifically Supported Wellness

The methods taught are backed by research from the Sadhguru Center for a Conscious Planet at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center – a teaching, research and clinical affiliate of Harvard Medical School. In 2023, the Sadhguru Center introduced these same techniques to Parkinson’s patients and is preparing to publish findings on their positive impact on mental health and emotional well-being.

Boxing 4 Balance is a non-contact, adapted boxing program designed specifically for individuals living with Parkinson’s disease. Sessions combine punching drills on heavy bags and focus mitts with footwork, balance training, core work, and functional strength exercises. The program includes elements of LSVT, boxing technique, and input from current research and our experienced physiotherapists. The goals of the program are to improve balance, gait, coordination, reaction time, strength, posture, vocal projection, and confidence — all areas commonly affected by Parkinson’s.

Classes are currently offered Mondays and Thursdays from 1:30-2:30pm at Action & Reaction MMA gym.

A medical clearance form must be completed and signed by a physician prior to enrollment. Please contact us at (416) 386-0384 or boxing@balancephysiotherapy.com to obtain this form
listings.expertise: Boxing 4 Balance classes are led and created by our Head Coach, Farnaz who is an experienced adapted boxing coach. She led boxing classes for PD in London, Ontario before moving to Toronto. She is an internationally trained Physiotherapist and currently also works as a Physiotherapy Assistant with clients with neurological conditions including PD. Classes are also led by Tracy Tan who is an experienced physiotherapist working with clients with PD. Prior to working with PD clients as a physiotherapist, Tracy completed a Master’s degree with her research focusing on proprioception and freezing of gait in PD. Her research has been published in scientific journals such as Neuroscience.

listings.name: CARESPACE Health + Wellness Clinics Fischer-Hallman
listings.description:
Support for people with Parkinson’s Disease. Under the guidance of program Director Dr. Quincy Almeida, the CARESPACE Parkinson Disease (and Neurodegenerative Disorder) Program brings together a dedicated team of multidisciplinary regulated health professionals who collaborate together to develop personalized coordinated health plans for people with Parkinson’s. Disease progression is measured and tracked using the Unified Parkinson’s Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS) and health plans are adjusted as required.

- Know where you’re at and track progression with a UPDRS score
- Get nutritional counselling and advice
- Help with sleep or lifestyle changes
- Psychotherapy for anxiety and depression
- Exercise prescription to reduce symptoms and slow progression
- Massage therapy
- Caregiver counselling and support
- Participate in PD SAFEx the clinically-proven exercise program for Parkinson’s Disease

Dr. Almeida leads a team of regulated health professionals including Physiotherapists, Kinesiologists, Chiropractors, Dietitians, Massage Therapists, Naturopathic Doctors, Counsellors and Social Workers. The team collaborates both together and with you to develop achievable goals. With coordinated care you can track your progression, get the best evidence-based advice and support with health plans personalized for your own unique situation. The Initial Assessment is an intensive hour and a half appointment with Dr. Almeida that will include taking your history and completing several assessments and analysis which will result in providing you with a baseline Unified Parkinson’s Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS) score. Based on the outcome, Dr. Almeida will provide personalized education* on topics such as drug interaction, food digestion and exercise. Where appropriate, he will also provide referrals to other members of the team for follow up visits.
listings.expertise: PD SAFEx technology is a set of sensory attention-focused exercises developed by Dr. Quincy Almeida, BSc, MSc, PhD who is the Director of the CARESPACE Health+Wellness Parkinson’s Program, was developed as a Professor at Wilfrid Laurier University, and the Director of the Movement and Disorder Research & Rehabilitation Centre (MDRC) in Waterloo Canada.

listings.expertise: I worked in Pharmaceutical Sales for many years promoting products for Parkinson's treatment and also had 2 friends with family members who had Parkinson's and who eventually passed away from it. The group ranged in age from 44 to 75. The 44-year-old woman was the one who had obtained the funding. That inspired me to run two 12 -week online fitness courses for adults with Parkinson's through Abbotsford House (part of the Glebe Centre) in Ottawa during Covid as well as one 12 -week course in person this past winter. I am also training an older adult with MS online and have been for more than 10 years. I have a BSC in Biochemistry and am a CanFitPro certified personal trainer with a number of certifications through CanFitPro for training older adults. I am very solution oriented, so I like to try to find a way for people to deal with their physical challenges "

listings.name: Cortex Physio and Rehab
listings.description: Cortex Physio and Rehab is proud to be the ONLY clinic in South-Western Ontario with a certified PWR!Moves therapist—offering hope, strength, and freedom of movement to those living with Parkinson’s Disease. listings.expertise:
At the Cummings Centre, a variety of programs are offered to enhance the quality of life for individuals living with Parkinson’s:

- Adapted Exercise Clinic: Twice-weekly exercise classes designed specifically for Parkinson’s, combining cardiovascular training with boxing, stability/balance, posture, and task-specific exercises. Clients must be assessed before registering to determine eligibility and the appropriate class. Classes run Monday to Friday.

listings.description:
Hamilton City Ballet’s Dance for Parkinson’s launched in 2013 with monthly classes and has evolved to weekly online classe! Our dance classes are inspired and shaped by the stories, music and choreography in ballets including The Nutcracker, Swan Lake and Don Quixote!
Join us Monday mornings for our seated dance class and Tuesday and Thursday evenings for our Stretch & Relaxation class, featuring The Franklin Method.
We are proud to be the first classical ballet program in Canada to offer Dance for Parkinson’s. Our teachers are proudly trained in the Dance for PD® pedagogy.
listings.expertise: All teaching faculty of Hamilton City Ballet’s Dance for Parkinson’s have participated in the Dance for PD® Teacher Training.

listings.name: Dance Nova Scotia
listings.description: Dance for Health: Seniors is a province-wide program of Dance Nova Scotia. Through this initiative, a network of 15 dance and movement instructors across Nova Scotia to offer regular in-person classes at the community level. Neurological research demonstrates that, in addition to moving the joints and toning the muscles, gentle dance movement to music, done on a regular basis, improves balance and gait, and can stabilize and even slow the progression of neurological conditions like Parkinson’s. For seniors living in remote and rural communities without easy access to a community class, an online version of our program will be available on YouTube by Spring 2024.
listings.expertise: All our community-based instructors have been trained by certified dance movement therapists with specialized knowledge and experience in dance as therapy for Parkinson’s and dementia. One of our advisors and master trainers, Dr. Rebecca Barnstaple, earned her PhD at York University investigating the neurobiological effects of dance, and is now mapping improvisatory movement practices and their medicinal properties as a postdoctoral fellow at the Institute for Critical Studies in Improvisation, University of Guelph.

listings.name: Dancing Parkinson’s YYC – Decidedly Jazz Danceworks
listings.description: Dancing Parkinson’s YYC provides dance classes for people with Parkinson’s disease. With live musical accompaniment and a focus on rhythm, body awareness, muscle development, coordination and socializing, the DPYYC classes have proven to be an uplifting and restorative experience for participants. We offer hybrid classes where participants have the option to attend class in person at Decidedly Jazz Danceworks or virtually through Zoom. Class starts with a seated warm up. Participants are given the option to move to a standing position assisted by a straight-backed chair or remain seated. Class finishes with moving around the room. No previous dance experience is required. Walkers, wheelchairs, canes and caregivers are welcome.
listings.expertise: Dancing Parkinson’s YYC was launched in 2013 as a pilot program by Anne Flynn (Professor Emerita, Dance, University of Calgary) and Vicki Adams Willis (Founder in Residence, DJD). The program now has ongoing connections with the University of Calgary, the Parkinson’s Association of Alberta, and actively participates in teaching and research programs. The DPYYC teaching and volunteer team is comprised of individuals with a wealth of experience in dance performance and education in a number of different genres.

Drawing on the lived experience and professional expertise of architects Duff Balmer and Robert Kastelic, both of whom have Parkinson’s, the resource shares practical ideas for designing and adapting homes to make everyday life easier, safer and more comfortable, while helping people maintain their independence and well-being.

listings.name: Diagnostic Imaginings
listings.description: Diagnostic Imaginings brings together people touched by Parkinson’s with musicians and dancers through creative processes based on the lived experiences of people with Parkinson’s and scientific research. Members of the community, including people living with Parkinson’s, loved ones, support workers, clinicians and researchers, are invited to take part in an artistic process based on their experiences with Parkinson’s. This process will be guided by artists Louise Campbell, Naila Kuhlmann and Rebecca Barnstaple with the aim of fostering creativity and well-being through arts participation, cultivating meaningful relationships between the artists and community members and facilitating knowledge and understanding of Parkinson’s in the wider Canadian public through artworks emerging from this project.

listings.name: Elder Care Transitions
listings.description:
Elder Care Transitions help seniors transition to senior living through a number of services.

We help you prepare a floor plan for your new suite, identifying with you items you wish take with you, and packing all of those belongings going to your new suite. We liaise between retirement residences including booking the elevator for move day. We also move those belongings and unpack them for you, setting it up exactly as you have stated on your floor plan.

Additional services: prepare remaining items for resale, content sales, pack items for donation, and deliver to a family or a chosen charity. We remove any unwanted furniture & belongings and can prepare you home for resale if required.

Supervise our in-house moving team. ECT does not subcontract the moving staff – our movers are part of ECT’s trusted team of professionals. Ensuring quality service is very important to us.

Making decisions about cherished items will go with you can be emotional. We understand the emotional attachment. We will take a gentle approach to assisting you with your downsizing needs.

ECT can also assist you with downsizing, decluttering, packing, and even real estate sales. We make change easy.”
listings.expertise: Elder Care Transitions has been in business with seniors for 18 years. Families and seniors do not have the luxury of spending the time needed to move someone. Let alone someone with over 60 years of items in their home. We have been trained with strategies and the assistance of talking to seniors with various conditions and meeting them where they are at.

listings.name: Fanny Bernstein Living Well with Parkinson’s Education and Exercise Program at North York General Hospital
listings.description:
Goal: to support care-partners & empower seniors with Parkinson’s to gain knowledge in disease management and to establish a “healthy brain” lifestyle to delay disease progression.

Services include:

(1) Individual consultation by: specialized pharmacist and/or physiotherapist

(2) Seniors with early stage of Parkinson’s disease (within 5 years of diagnosis) may join the 8-week group education and exercise.

Topics covered include but are not limited to:

Overview of Parkinson’s disease and coping with the diagnosis
Recognition and treatment of motor and non-motor symptoms
Education on cognitive function, diet, and speech & swallowing
Mindfulness and relaxation training
Advanced care planning and community resources
listings.expertise: The program is presented by the inter-professional team with many years of experience working with people with Parkinson’s. listings.expertise: We have worked with clients living with Parkinson’s disease for over 7 years and have immersed ourselves in the community. Also have had lunch and learn presentations on the importance of exercise for Parkinson’s disease symptoms. We have also attended many Parkinson’s conferences to offer support and knowledge to those in attendance.

listings.name: Flutter Speech and Literacy Services
listings.description: The SPEAK OUT!® Therapy Program by Parkinson Voice Project is a specialized speech therapy approach for people with Parkinson’s disease. It helps individuals speak more clearly and confidently by strengthening the muscles used for speech and swallowing and by encouraging purposeful, intentional speech. The program focuses on improving voice volume, clarity, and overall communication for daily life, with ongoing practice to help maintain progress over time. Afterwards, participants join a Speak Out! Therapy Group to participate in weekly. Groups are free or donation-based and are open to anyone who has completed the Speak Out! Program with a speech therapist.
listings.expertise:
I am a speech-language pathology clinician with foundational training in working with individuals with Parkinson’s disease through graduate-level coursework, completion of the SPEAK OUT!® training course, and clinical placement experience. While my direct clinical experience with Parkinson’s disease is developing, I am committed to evidence-based practice, ongoing professional learning, and providing individualized, supportive therapy focused on functional communication goals. I aim to include family support in the care of all my clients, to ensure a comprehensive therapy journey.

Services available in Turkish and English.

listings.expertise:
Sarah Martens has been working with people with Parkinson’s since the spring of 2020, after private studies with movement and dance therapist, Samantha Emanuel. listings.name: Fusion Psychological Services
listings.description:
Assessment services include psychodiagnostic and mental health assessments, neuropsychological and cognitive assessments, adult neurodiversity assessments for ADHD and autism, concussion and neurological concerns, learning and disability assessments, psychoeducational assessments, trauma and PTSD, and gender-affirming surgical-readiness second-assessor services. Assessments may help clarify diagnosis, cognitive functioning, treatment needs, accommodations, and practical recommendations for daily life, work, or education.

Psychotherapy services are tailored to each client’s needs, circumstances, and interpersonal style. Areas of support include anxiety and stress, depression and grief, trauma and PTSD, OCD symptoms, relationship concerns, neurodiversity, sexuality and gender, workplace stress, burnout, emotion regulation, self-esteem, and general mental health concerns.
Treatment may incorporate evidence-based approaches including Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT), Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT), Dialectical Behaviour Therapy (DBT), Emotion-Focused Therapy (EFT), Internal Family Systems-informed approaches, psychodynamic therapy, and mindfulness-based interventions. Care is collaborative and considers biological, psychological, interpersonal, and social factors when developing treatment recommendations and goals.
listings.expertise: I am a doctoral-level neuropsychologist with specialized training in brain-behaviour relationships, having completed a pre-doctoral internship in neuropsychology and holding registration in Clinical Neuropsychology with the College of Psychologists and Behavioural Analysts of Ontario (CPBAO). My experience working with Parkinson's disease encompasses a thorough understanding of its clinical presentation, motor features, and neurocognitive sequelae, including mild cognitive impairment, Lewy body dementia, and Parkinson's disease dementia. I am skilled in administering and interpreting standardized neuropsychological test batteries tailored to PD, carefully accounting for variables such as bradykinesia, tremor, fatigue, dopaminergic medication timing (on versus off states), and age-related normative data, and I can differentiate PD-related cognitive changes from other etiologies including Alzheimer's dementia, vascular cognitive impairment, depression, medication effects, and reversible causes. In my practice I provide psychoeducation, cognitive rehabilitation strategies, and behavioural interventions to address mood, anxiety, sleep disturbances, impulse control disorders related to dopamine agonists, and caregiver support. I collaborate closely with neurologists, movement disorder specialists, geriatricians, occupational therapists, and speech-language pathologists to inform treatment planning, medication management decisions, and functional capacity assessments, and I maintain my expertise through ongoing engagement with PD-focused research, continuing professional development on evolving pharmacological and surgical treatments such as DBS candidacy, and familiarity with current diagnostic criteria.

listings.name: Henninger Speech and Language Centre
listings.description: Our services include an assessment that includes gathering of an extensive case history and an evaluation of vocal function and swallowing, if needed. An ENT referral is sometimes made before beginning any therapy, in particular, if vocal quality is significantly compromised. Assessment findings will determine if the individual is a good candidate for treatment and which treatment approach best fits their needs and profile. The treatment protocols offered include SPEAK OUT! and LSVT Loud. SPEAK OUT!, developed by the Parkinson’s Voice Project, focuses on producing a stronger, clearer voice. It is based on the concept of intent and strengthens the muscles used for speaking and swallowing. SPEAK OUT! is comprised of an assessment session and 12 treatment sessions. Clients attend 45-minute sessions, 3 times per week for 4 consecutive weeks, and complete daily home practice. Once treatment is complete, the Parkinson’s Voice Project hold LOUD crowd groups and free Facebook practice sessions. This is essential for maintaining the gains achieved in therapy. Lee Silverman Voice Treatment (LSVT) is an intensive treatment protocol that supports people with Parkinson’s disease to improve vocal loudness and clarity. It is comprised of an assessment session and 16 treatment sessions. Clients attend 1-hour sessions 4 times per week for 4 consecutive weeks and complete daily practice at home.
listings.expertise: Our speech-language pathologist, Lynn Mark, has been working with individuals with Parkinson’s disease for over 12 years. She is certified in both Lee Silverman Voice Treatment (LSVT) and SPEAK OUT! therapy protocols.

This may help people with Parkinson’s improve the day to day quality of their lives, and manage challenging symptoms more effectively.

Mime techniques are fun, easy to learn, highly customizable, require no specialized equipment and can be performed anywhere and at any time. Circus Games are also used to help strengthen large motor skills, balance and flexibility, while also having fun.
listings.expertise: Our founder, Barbara Salsberg Mathews, MEd., was diagnosed with Parksinson’s Disease in 2020. She regularly participates in various PD research studies. She is on Canadian Open Parkinson’s Network’s advisory committee and one of the creators of The Dopamine Dance movement. Barbara helps produce resources for Parkinson’s Europe and The Michael J Fox Foundation. The Mime Over Mind program is an exemplar course through University of Guelph’s new Bachelor of Creative Arts Health and Wellness degree. Barbara has been training trainers through this program.

listings.description: NeuroGym® has over 30 years of experience treating individuals with neurological injuries and conditions. Our active, evidence-based approach and patented technology allow patients to take action in their own recovery. Whenever possible, the patient, not the therapist, initiates movement, which can help rewire the brain and speed up recovery. When patient-initiated movement is challenging, we use our innovative techniques and tools to help enable motor recovery when it would otherwise be difficult or impossible to accomplish.
listings.expertise: When it comes to Parkinson’s Disease, NeuroGym® can offer a wealth of expertise. listings.name: Neurology Rehab
listings.description:
Neurology Rehab is a specialized clinic dedicated to treating individuals with Parkinson’s disease and other movement disorders. Our mission is to improve access to expert, compassionate care for those living with neurological conditions.
We offer:

- 1-on-1 Physiotherapy: Tailored, evidence-based treatments to enhance mobility, balance, and overall function.
- Parkinson’s-Specific Exercise Coaching: Custom programs designed to address the unique movement challenges of Parkinson’s, building strength, flexibility, and confidence.
- Parkinson’s Consultation: Comprehensive assessments to provide personalized strategies for managing symptoms.
- Care Partner Training: Practical guidance and education to empower care partners in supporting their loved ones and maximizing independence.
- Online Parkinson’s Education Courses: Accessible, on-demand resources to help individuals take control of their Parkinson’s.

At Neurology Rehab, we are fully dedicated to helping patients with Parkinson’s and other movement disorders achieve their goals and improve their quality of life through specialized care.
listings.expertise:
Haseel Bhatt is a physiotherapist with over 15 years of experience specializing in Parkinson’s care. He was trained at the Parkinson Center of Excellence in the UK and the Toronto Movement Disorders Clinic and holds advanced certifications in PWR! (Parkinson Wellness Recovery), LSVT BIG, and Allied Health Team Training for Parkinson’s Disease.

Haseel is also an adjunct lecturer at the University of Toronto and a member of the Parkinson’s Foundation Physical Therapy Faculty program. He integrates the latest evidence-based therapies into his practice to ensure the highest quality care.

Whether newly diagnosed or living with Parkinson’s for years, Haseel is committed to helping individuals achieve their goals, build confidence, and develop personalized plans to live more active, fulfilling lives.

listings.name: NeuroMotrix
listings.description: Specialized in adapted physical activity, the NeuroMotrix team has made it its mission to improve the quality of life of people living with a neurological disorder (Parkinson’s disease, Alzheimer’s disease, multiple sclerosis, post-stroke, cognitive decline, chronic pain, lack of balance, osteoporosis, osteoarthritis, chronic fatigue, etc.) or related symptoms. Neither illness nor age should prevent a person from enjoying the universal benefits of physical activity. In order to meet the specific needs of each individual, the NeuroMotrix team has developed an approach that bridges the gap between science and practice. NeuroMotrix kinesiologist start every new consultation with a physical evaluation to observe your capacities and limitations, and discuss your history, so your exercise program his tailored to your functional needs and interest. You can choose to train with your kinesiologist as many time as needed, in person or by virtual means. Working with a health professional as a positive impact on your training’s consistency and efficiency, and sense of security.
listings.expertise: The co-founder’s of NeuroMotrix met in 2015 in a research laboratory, as they collaborate on the feasibility of physical activity based-study with a Parkinson population. From there, they have expand there one-on-one service to wide collaboration with regional associations like : Parkinson Quebec, Parkinson Montreal-Laval, Parkinson Monteregie, Parkinson Quebec Basses-Laurentides, and many more. Services vary from personal training session, to group activities like Adapted Boxing and Nordic Walking, and online training sessions for the regional associations.

listings.name: NeuroThrive Education Consultancy

Physiotherapists use hands-on therapy, exercises, stretches, and more to help people address their unique challenges and concerns. PAA is pleased to work with registered physiotherapists Cari Cooke (Edmonton) and Jackie Townsend (Calgary) to offer 1:1 appointments at both our Calgary and Edmonton office locations. Receipts will be provided as physical therapy is a health expense from a tax perspective and may be covered by your insurance.
listings.expertise:
For more than 40 years, Parkinson Association of Alberta has been the source for support, education and advocacy for individuals and families affected by Parkinson disease.

Parkinson Association of Alberta provides emotional, practical, educational and active support for people living with and caring for someone affected by Parkinson disease or Parkinson’s Plus Syndromes.

listings.name: Parkinson Association of Alberta - Circuit
listings.description: Two program levels – Circuit I is our high-intensity Challenging level, while Circuit II is our Moderate level. Both programs focus on a circuit of exercises to build strength, improve cardio and overall fitness. Please note an assessment may be required to participate in this program.

listings.name: Parkinson Montréal Laval
listings.description: We offer social, support and sporting activities to people living with Parkinson’s and their care partners. We offer a monthly support group (French) for people living with Parkinson’s and a monthly support group for care partners (French). We offer information sessions for newly diagnosed patients and their care partners. We offer many conferences, discussion groups and other information sessions.
listings.expertise:
Parkinson Montreal-Laval is a non-profit organization established in 2004 for the Parkinson’s community based in Montreal and Laval.
We offer some activities and services with specialized teachers and psychosocial workers.

listings.name: Parkinson Society British Columbia - Vernon Support Group
listings.description:
Join this group to connect with fellow people with Parkinson’s and their care partners.

Support Groups are led by volunteer facilitators, both in-person and virtually. All are designed to provide a safe, comfortable place for people to connect and share with each other on how to live well with Parkinson’s.
listings.expertise: Founded in 1969, Parkinson Society British Columbia is a non-profit organization dedicated to empowering the Parkinson’s community by providing resources and services to enable self-management, self-reliance, and self-advocacy. They support individuals with Parkinson’s and their loved ones through one-on-one consultations, free short-term counselling, healthcare navigation, virtual physiotherapy, support groups, educational seminars and workshops, and the PD Link peer support program. The Society also advocates for improved care, produces informational materials, offers specialized training for healthcare professions, and funds research to advance treatments.

We use a holistic approach to rehabilitation with an emphasis on client-centered treatment, research, education, community engagement that can help clients maximize their mobility and improve their performance in daily activity. Our therapists have post-graduate training to specialize in neurological rehabilitation, including the Bobath Concept and NDT (Neurodevelopmental Treatment), and experience helping people with Parkinson’s Disease.
listings.expertise: David has been treating people with Parkinson’s Disease since becoming a Physiotherapist in 2011.

listings.description: Our combination of in-person and online group training programs helps our community of people living with Parkinson’s move around inside and outside the gym more safely. We’re not training for championship belts, we’re training to be able to pick up grandchildren, pet a dog, play a round of golf or pick up laundry from the floor. listings.name: Rhythmic Rehab Inc.
listings.description: At Rhythmic Rehab we provide neurologic rehabilitation services across the lifespan in-home in Cambridge, ON and online Ontario wide. We specialize in Neurologic Music Therapy®, an evidence-based clinical treatment system used to train and retrain non-musical brain behavior and function in the domains of cognition, sensorimotor and speech and language. We help patients with Parkinson’s disease maintain cognitive function, normalize walking, strengthen motor movements and improve voice quality and intelligibility. Sessions may include listening and moving to music, singing and songwriting or instrument playing. No prior musical experience is required to participate!
listings.expertise: Kaitlyn is a certified Music Therapist (MTA) and Neurologic Music Therapy® Fellow (NMT-F™). She has experience working with patients with Parkinson’s disease in hospital and community settings.

listings.name: Right at Home Canada - Vancouver Northshore
listings.description:
At Right at Home North Shore & Tri-Cities, we provide compassionate, RN-led home care services designed to help older adults and individuals living with Parkinson's disease remain safe, comfortable, and independent in their own homes.

Our team understands the unique challenges that Parkinson's can present, including mobility changes, fall risks, medication management, cognitive changes, fatigue, and the need for consistent daily routines. We work closely with clients, families, and healthcare providers to develop personalized care plans that evolve with changing needs.

Our services include:

Personal care assistance (bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting)
Medication reminders and support
Mobility and transfer assistance
Fall prevention and safety monitoring
Companionship and social engagement
Meal preparation and nutrition support
Light housekeeping and laundry
Transportation and accompaniment to appointments
Respite care for family caregivers
Dementia and cognitive support
Hospital-to-home transition support
24/7 and overnight care options

As a locally owned and operated home care provider, we offer free in-home care assessments and ongoing support from experienced nursing professionals. Our goal is to enhance quality of life, promote independence, and provide peace of mind for individuals and families navigating Parkinson's disease and other complex health conditions.

listings.name: Rock Steady Boxing - Niagara on the Lake
listings.description: Our mission is to improve the physical and mental capacity of people living with Parkinson's disease through exercise and social connection. Rock Steady Boxing is an exercise program designed specifically for those with Parkinson's, and participants often report a better quality of life as they become stronger, faster, and more agile in their daily activities. We also offer a free trial period so each person can determine whether the program is a good fit for them.
listings.expertise: I have worked with clients living with Parkinson's disease since 2013. In 2016, I founded Rock Steady Boxing Niagara, where I serve as head coach. The program began with seven members and has since grown to more than forty.

listings.expertise: Coaches are exercise professionals including registered kinesiologist, exercise physiologist, and certified personal trainers. Coaches are certified through the Rock Steady Boxing organization.

listings.description: Rock Steady Boxing is a non-contact boxing program that uses boxing techniques to help people with Parkinson’s disease improve their quality of life through a non-contact boxing curriculum. listings.name: Rock Steady Boxing York Region
listings.description:
Rock Steady Boxing York Region is a unique exercise program based on the Rock Steady Boxing Method. Inspired by training used by professional boxers and adapted for people with Parkinson’s, the program combines regular exercise, strength training, stretching, jogging, balance work, vocal strengthening, and non-contact boxing.

These boxing and conditioning drills are designed to help participants manage Parkinson’s symptoms and support a better quality of life. Along the way, members work hard, have fun, and build friendships.

“I have been attending Rock Steady Boxing classes with Melissa since 2017. It’s a great workout and has helped my balance and strength training. I do three classes a week and look forward to each session. More importantly, it has given me a real sense of community. Over the years, I’ve met so many fellow boxers who are fighting the same battle against Parkinson’s”— Alex
listings.expertise:
Melissa and her team have worked with and taught people living with Parkinson’s since 2017. She is a certified Rock Steady Boxing instructor and is also a yoga & Chi Gong instructor. She has also served on the Vaughan SuperWalk Committee helping raise funds and awareness for Parkinson's.

Please contact Melissa for a consultation and assessment.

listings.description: Rockland Rural Rehab offers in-home physiotherapy services across rural communities and the Ottawa area, supporting individuals who face transportation barriers to clinic-based care. Services focus on improving mobility, balance, strength, and functional movement through individualized, evidence-based treatment. The physiotherapist has extensive experience working with individuals living with Parkinson’s and completed LSVT BIG training in January 2026, further strengthening evidence-based movement and functional rehabilitation approaches
listings.expertise:
Swetha has worked with people living with Parkinson’s since 2008 in both community, long term care and clinic environments. Swetha’s physiotherapy experience includes supporting balance, mobility, flexibility, and functional movement through individualized treatment programs designed to meet each client’s goals and abilities.

Services are available in English, Hindi, and Kannada.

listings.name: Savage Yoga
listings.description: Savage Yoga offers accessible, adaptable yoga and yoga therapy for people living with Parkinson’s disease and other movement-related challenges. Practices can be modified for different levels of mobility and may include chair-based or supported movement, gentle strengthening, balance and mobility work, breathing practices, relaxation, and meditation. Sessions are designed to meet people where they are, with an emphasis on safety, choice, dignity, and building confidence in movement. Individual and small-group sessions are available in person in Saint John, NB.
listings.expertise:
I am a registered Yoga Therapist (C-IAYT) and experienced yoga educator with a focus on accessible, adaptable practices for people with varying mobility, strength, balance, and movement needs. I hold E-RYT 500, YACEP, RCYT and RPYT credentials, as well as certifications in Yin, Restorative Yoga and Ayurveda.

Through Savage Yoga, I have worked with clients who experience mobility limitations and other physical challenges, adapting yoga practices to individual abilities and needs. My approach emphasizes functional movement, balance, mobility, strength, breathwork, relaxation, and maintaining autonomy and confidence in movement.

I am committed to continuing my education around Parkinson’s Disease and to providing an inclusive environment where practices can be modified for the individual, including the use of chairs, props, and other supports when appropriate.

listings.description: Senior Helpers support clients living with Parkinson’s by assisting with daily activities such as mobility, personal care, meal preparation, and medication reminders. Caregivers help reduce fall risks, provide steady support during movement, and encourage routines that promote independence, dignity, and safety at home.
listings.expertise: Senior helpers has been in business since 2002. We have over 400 locations worldwide. One of the things we offer is in home support for Parkinson’s.

listings.name: Senior Helpers of Victoria
listings.description: Senior Helpers Victoria provides specialized Parkinson's-informed in-home care that enables people living with Parkinson's to remain safe, independent, and engaged in the comfort of their own homes. Our caregivers support personal care, mobility, transfers, medication reminders, meal preparation, transportation, companionship, exercise encouragement, cognitive cueing, executive functioning support, respite for care partners, and daily routines. Every client receives an individualized care plan tailored to their goals, symptoms, and stage of Parkinson's. We work collaboratively with families and healthcare professionals to promote safety, dignity, independence, and quality of life while helping clients age in place with confidence.
listings.expertise: Senior Helpers Victoria has extensive experience supporting individuals living with Parkinson's disease across a wide range of stages and care needs. Our specialized Parkinson's Care Program was developed in collaboration with Becky Dunlop, a Parkinson's educator and internationally recognized specialist in Parkinson's care, to ensure our approach reflects current best practices and the unique challenges associated with the condition. Our caregivers are supported through Parkinson's-specific education and provide individualized assistance with mobility, transfers, freezing episodes, fall prevention, medication reminder routines, personal care, cognitive cueing, executive functioning support, fatigue management, transportation, and meaningful daily engagement. Every client receives a customized care plan that evolves with their changing needs, and we work collaboratively with families and healthcare professionals to promote safety, dignity, independence, and quality of life while helping individuals remain successfully in their own homes.

listings.name: Senior Helpers Toronto
listings.description: Senior Helpers is honored to lead the industry in programs like Senior Gems, which certifies our caregivers in Alzheimer’s and Dementia care, as well as our first-in-the-industry Parkinson’s Care Program, delivering specialized training to our caregivers who help those with Parkinson’s. The Senior Gems program is based on GEMS, techniques, strategies, and overall approach to care, created and developed by Teepa Snow, Positive Approach, LLC, Teepa snow.com. With Senior Helpers in-home care, you can feel secure your loved one is in good hands.
listings.expertise: Since 2002, Senior Helpers has been a North American leader in professional, in-home senior assistance services. Seeing a rapid increase of seniors in Canada, projected to grow up to 25% of the total population by 2036, it’s our mission to help seniors remain in their homes despite age-related illnesses and mobility challenges. Senior Helpers has cared for tens of thousands with a pledge to provide care and comfort at a moments notice. We’ve built a reputation on providing the best in dependable, consistent and affordable non-medical senior care services.

listings.name: Shoreline Therapy
listings.description:
Our clinic provides Speech-Language Therapy and Occupational Therapy services to people living with Parkinson’s disease. Our clinicians are certified in Lee Silverman Voice Treatment (LSVT) LOUD and LSVT BIG, two intensive, evidence-based treatment programs designed to address the communication and movement challenges associated with Parkinson’s disease.

We also offer non-intensive treatment options tailored to each individual’s needs, goals, and preferences. Speech-Language Therapy services may include individual speech and voice therapy, voice groups, and facilitating access to augmentative and alternative communication (AAC). Occupational Therapy services may include recommendations for adaptive equipment to support participation in daily activities, as well as strategies for managing fatigue and conserving energy throughout the day.
listings.expertise:
Pamela Coulter is a registered Speech-Language Pathologist who is certified to provide LSVT-LOUD treatment. Pamela has worked in the field of speech-language pathology since 2007, and has worked with people living with Parkinson's disease throughout this time.
Shalyn Henley is a registered Occupational Therapist (N.S.) who is certified to provide LSVT-BIG treatment. Shalyn has been working as a registered occupational therapist since 2025, and has worked with people living with Parkinson's disease in acute care and rehabilitation environments.

listings.name: Signature Therapy and Rehabilitation

- Parkinsonism
- Progressive Supranuclear Palsy
- Multiple System Atrophy
- Essential Tremor
- And others!

- Consultation, assessment, and treatment. Options include individualized therapy programs, family education and communication training, group treatment, SPEAK OUT!®, LSVT LOUD®, and more!
- Evening and weekend appointments to fit your schedule
- FREE no-obligation education sessions with Parkinson Wellness Projects
- Resources and ongoing support throughout your diagnosis

We are actively accepting new clients, and we offer free initial consultations. Let’s SpeakSTRONG together!
listings.expertise: Jasmine Cload is a registered Speech-Language Pathologist (SLP) who provides speech and swallowing services for people living with Parkinson Disease and other neurological movement diagnoses. Jasmine helped create British Columbia’s first full-time public SLP program for Parkinson Disease, and she is also the founder of SpeakSTRONG. Jasmine has completed additional training with Parkinson’s Foundation, and is one of ten Pan-American clinicians selected by the International Parkinson and Movement Disorders Society (MDS) to be a Parkinson Disease trainer for other healthcare professionals. Jasmine is the first Canadian chosen by the International Society to receive this advanced training. Jasmine is a certified provider of both Lee Silverman Voice Treatment (LSVT LOUD®) and SPEAK OUT!® treatment programs, for which she has received the Parkinson Voice Project® grant three years in a row. Jasmine has provided a variety of education seminars and workshops to hospital teams, professionals, support groups, and the public. Jasmine is a clinical educator with the University of British Columbia, and she is a volunteer member of the Adult Services Committee with Speech and Hearing BC. listings.name: The Wellness Institute at Seven Oaks General Hospital
listings.description:
NeuroFit is an 8-week exercise program for adults living with neurological conditions. Led by a Clinical Exercise Physiologist, participants attend two supervised classes per week to improve strength, balance, mobility, endurance, and confidence through safe exercise. An initial Physiotherapy Assessment ensures individualized programming.

Suitable for individuals with Parkinson's disease, Multiple Sclerosis, Stroke, Guillane-Barr© syndrome, Huntington's Disease and other neurological conditions.

To help ensure this program is safe and effective, participants must meet the following participation guidelines:
1. Have a 1:1 Physiotherapy intake appointment at the Wellness Institute to evaluate abilities and limitations.
2. Be able to walk independently, with or without a walking aide, or be accompanied by an attendant.
3. Have the physical ability to actively participate in the exercise session for 45 minutes.
4. Be able to pay attention, follow instructions and mimic exercises. They must be aware of their safe bounds of ability.
5. Be able to manage their own bladder function.
6. Have completed a rehabilitation program after a stroke.
listings.expertise: As a certified medical fitness facility, we have extensive experience supporting individuals with Parkinson's disease and other neurological conditions. Our physiotherapists are trained in neurological assessment and provide comprehensive evaluations to guide safe, individualized care. Exercise sessions are led by a Clinical Exercise Physiologist with years of experience delivering evidence-based programming through our NeuroFit program, helping participants improve strength, balance, mobility, and overall function in a safe, supportive environment.

listings.expertise:
My background is in visual arts from the Academy of Fine Arts of Brera in Milan, where the artistic tradition is deeply connected to the idea of the “wounded healer,” inspired by the myth of Chiron. This perspective views creative practice as a way to transform vulnerability and lived experience into meaningful expression.

Through accessible materials such as paper, drawing, and sculptural processes, participants are invited to explore gesture, movement, and imagination. The focus is not on artistic skill, but on the process itself: slowing down, experimenting, and finding moments of emotional relief and personal agency through art.

These sessions can be adapted for individuals with Parkinson’s, for care partners, or for mixed groups, creating spaces where creativity supports both personal reflection and shared experience.
